rationale: Comprehensive cohort characterization of NKX6-2-related disorder demonstrates that epilepsy is not obligately coupled to diffuse cerebral hypomyelination. Chelban et al. (2020) evaluated 11 novel patients across 8 families alongside previously published cases, explicitly noting the occurrence of phenotypes exhibiting epilepsy in the absence of overt cerebral hypomyelination, as well as cases demonstrating diffuse cerebral hypomyelination without seizures. None of the available literature establishes a strict co-segregation between epilepsy and diffuse hypomyelination.

evidence.text: In an expanded international cohort study, comprehensive phenotypic and neuroimaging analysis established that epilepsy can occur in the absence of overt hypomyelination, and conversely diffuse hypomyelination can occur without seizures in NKX6-2-related disorder.

source.title: Genetic and phenotypic characterization of NKX6‐2‐related spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: The phenotypic and neuroimaging expression in NKX6-2 is described and it is shown that phenotypes with epilepsy in the absence of overt hypomyelination and diffuse hypomyelination without seizures can occur.

numbers.metric: new cases identified from eight families

evidence.text: Initial identification of NKX6-2 mutations in early-onset spastic ataxia demonstrated clinical and radiological heterogeneity, where some affected families presented with childhood onset and cerebellar atrophy without prominent initial hypomyelination, while others demonstrated early-onset spastic ataxia with diffuse hypomyelination.

source.title: Mutations in NKX6-2 Cause Progressive Spastic Ataxia and Hypomyelination
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: Affected members of two families had childhood onset disease with very slow progression. They are still alive in their 30s and 40s and show predominant ataxia and cerebellar atrophy features on imaging. Affected members of the third family had a similar but earlier-onset presentation associated with brain hypomyelination.

numbers.metric: affected individuals reported across three families

evidence.text: Review of hypomyelinating leukodystrophies indicates that truncating variants in NKX6-2 are associated with severe Pelizaeus-Merzbacher-like disease presentations with severe hypomyelination, where some patients present with severe epilepsy.

source.title: Hypomyelinating leukodystrophies—Unravelling myelin biology
source.quote: Truncating variants in NKX6-2 cause a severe form of PMLD, ... hypomyelination, some patients have severe epilepsy

new_directions.question_text: What underlying cellular or network pathomechanisms cause epileptogenesis in NKX6-2 deficiency independently of myelination defects?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether NKX6-2 functions in interneuron differentiation or cortical excitability will explain seizure susceptibility in patients without overt MRI hypomyelination.

new_directions.question_text: Do specific missense variants in the NKX6-2 homeodomain alter seizure risk differently compared to truncating or loss-of-function variants across all reported cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Systematic genotype-phenotype meta-analysis mapping variant classes to EEG anomalies and seizure semiology would improve diagnostic and prognostic stratification.
